assumptions: The aligned block is real homology; the clamp is back-translated through the codon table named.
limits: Both original CODEHOP servers are gone and no runnable oracle exists, so every number is recomputed in the test by a path that does not call the engine's own predicates.
Designs primers; it does not predict which homologues amplify.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which hybrid degenerate-core primers does a block of aligned protein give, for homologues too diverged for nucleotide design?

description: Design CODEHOP hybrid oligos from a block of aligned PROTEIN - for homologues too diverged for nucleotide-level design to see at all. Each primer is a 3' DEGENERATE core over a few conserved residues fused to a 5' non-degenerate consensus clamp, back-translated through a codon-usage table. A different algorithm from the degenerate designer, not a variant of it.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

alignment.description: the ALIGNED PROTEIN rows, each { name, sequence } in one-letter amino acids with gaps preserved - wire an upstream protein alignment here. At least 3 sequences: the clamp is a CONSENSUS, and two have none worth the name.

alignment_fasta.description: an aligned PROTEIN FASTA, when there is no upstream alignment to wire.

base_cutoff.description: minimum predicted probability for a base to enter the degenerate core. Advanced.

block_index.description: which gapless block to design in, 0-based, ordered as `gaplessBlocks` returns them (blocks of at least 8 ungapped columns). Unset = the first.

clamp_tm.description: target melting temperature for the non-degenerate 5' clamp (Rose 2003 step 8: "the current default is 60 °C, which usually provides a clamp of ~20 nucleotides"), measured as nearest-neighbour Tm in the buffer `conditions` names. In °C.

conditions.description: salt, magnesium, dNTP and oligo concentrations plus the salt-correction method and any additives the clamp Tm is measured in. Left unset it is filled from your reaction-conditions settings, and falls back to pydna's Taq defaults (SantaLucia & Hicks 2004 table, 250 nM primer, Owczarzy 2008 salt correction) when there are none. Advanced.

additives.description: DMSO and formamide, applied AFTER the nearest-neighbour Tm.

DMSOfactor.description: °C of Tm lost per % DMSO, as an explicit override. Supplying it WINS over `dmsoMethod`, and detaches the number from its citation.

dmsoMethod.description: which published DMSO depression sets the coefficient. Values: ahs01 (Ahsen et al. (2001) (0.75 °C per %)), mus81 (Musielski et al. (1981) (0.6 °C per %)), cul76 (Cullen and Bick (1976) (0.5 °C per %)), esc80 (Escara and Hutton (1980) (0.675 °C per %)).

fmd.description: formamide — percent when `fmdmethod` is 1, molar when it is 2.

fmdfactor.description: °C lost per % formamide (method 1). Papers report 0.6 to 0.72.

fmdmethod.description: 1 = linear % formamide (McConaughy 1969) · 2 = GC-dependent, molar (Blake & Delcourt 1996). Values: 1 (Linear %, McConaughy 1969), 2 (GC-dependent molar, Blake & Delcourt 1996).

method.description: which validated nearest-neighbour model and default buffer — santaLucia (pydna `tm_default`, Taq) or dbd (pydna `tm_dbd`, Phusion / Pfu-Sso7d). Values: santaLucia (SantaLucia (pydna tm_default, Taq)), dbd (DNA-binding domain (pydna tm_dbd, Phusion)).

nnTable.description: override the method's nearest-neighbour table; the buffer convention is unchanged.

saltcorr.description: Biopython salt-correction method 0–7 (0 = none). It moves the answer more than any other knob here: on a 24-mer at the Taq buffer the eight span 79.302 °C (method 0) to 66.009 °C (method 2).

selfcomp.description: both strands are one self-complementary oligo (the concentration term becomes dnac1 rather than dnac1 − dnac2/2).

core_lengths.description: core lengths the scan tries, in residues — every length here is scanned and the best-scoring core kept. Advanced.

genetic_code_id.description: NCBI `transl_table` id for the codon-to-residue map. Advanced.

max_clamp_length.description: ceiling on clamp growth, so an unreachable Tm REFUSES instead of consuming the whole block. Ours, and a stop condition rather than a published criterion - 40 nt is already twice the ~20 the paper expects. In nt. Advanced.

max_core_degeneracy.description: degeneracy ceiling for the 3' core (Rose 2003 step 7: "a maximum degeneracy of 128").

max_run.description: longest single-base run allowed; 2003's stated polynucleotide run limit. A primer exceeding it is rejected. In nt. Advanced.

strand.description: which strand to design on. `both` returns forward and reverse sets, which is what a PCR needs.

table.description: the codon-usage table to back-translate the clamp through, BY NAME as the Codon Usage panel lists it. REQUIRED and deliberately without a default: a CODEHOP designed under the wrong organism's usage is wrong in a way nothing downstream can detect, so picking one here would silently pick a host (§1).

weighting.description: how the alignment's rows are weighted before the core's consensus is read. Values: pb (Position-based (Henikoff & Henikoff 1994)), none (None — every row counts once). Advanced.

name: design_codehop

blockCount.description: how many gapless blocks the alignment offers, so a caller can see there were others to choose

forward.description: the first forward oligo, clamp + core

primers.description: the designed oligos: each with its degenerate 3' core, its consensus 5' clamp, the residues it covers and its degeneracy

rejections.description: why each candidate position was rejected - degeneracy, run length, or a clamp that could not reach the Tm

table.description: which codon table the clamp was back-translated through, named so a design is never unattributable
